title: Ski Downhill Fish Run
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a ski downhill game using Three.js. The player controls a fish (loaded from 'BarramundiFish.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN) skiing down a procedurally generated snowy slope.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera (FOV 60) positioned behind and above the fish, following it as it moves downhill.
- Add a directional light (white, intensity 1.2) from upper-left, and ambient light (0x8888cc, intensity 0.5) for a cold mountain feel.
- Create a long sloped plane (at least 500 units long, 40 units wide) textured or colored white (0xf0f0ff) to represent the ski slope. The slope should descend along the negative Z axis with a gentle downward angle (about 15 degrees).
- Load the fish model 'BarramundiFish.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to roughly 1.5 units. This is the player's ski character. Place it at the top of the slope at position (0, 0.5, 0).
- Generate 20 obstacle trees (simple green cones on brown cylinders) randomly placed along the slope at Z positions between -30 and -450, X positions between -15 and 15.
- Generate 10 collectible golden rings (yellow torus geometry, emissive 0xffaa00) scattered along the slope similarly.
- Add a finish line at Z = -480 (a red rectangular plane spanning the width of the slope).

## Physics & Movement
- The fish automatically slides downhill at an increasing speed. Start at speed 0 and accelerate at 0.02 units/frame up to a max speed of 1.5 units/frame.
- Left/Right arrow keys (or A/D) steer the fish left/right at 0.15 units per frame. Clamp X position to [-18, 18].
- Spacebar applies a brake, reducing current speed by 30% each frame it's held (minimum speed 0.2).
- Collision detection: if the fish comes within 1.5 units of a tree obstacle, it counts as a crash. On crash, reduce speed to 0.1 and increment crash counter. The tree should disappear (or turn red).
- Ring collection: if the fish comes within 2.0 units of a ring, collect it (remove ring from scene, increment score).
- When the fish crosses Z <= -480, the game ends. Show 'FINISH!' on the HUD.

## HUD / UI
- Display at top-left: 'Speed: X.XX' showing current speed.
- Display at top-center: 'Score: N / 10' showing collected rings.
- Display at top-right: 'Crashes: N' showing crash count.
- Display a 'Start' button (id='startBtn') centered on screen. Clicking it begins the game (fish starts moving).
- When game ends, display 'FINISH! Final Score: N' in a large overlay div (id='finishOverlay').
- Add a 'Restart' button (id='restartBtn') visible only after finishing.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- gameStarted: boolean (true after Start clicked)
- gameFinished: boolean (true when fish crosses finish)
- speed: number (current speed, 2 decimal places)
- playerX: number (fish X position)
- playerZ: number (fish Z position)
- score: number (rings collected, 0-10)
- crashes: number (crash count)
- totalObstacles: number (should be 20)
- totalRings: number (should be 10 initially)
- ringsRemaining: number (rings still in scene)
- braking: boolean (true while space held)
- fishModelLoaded: boolean (true once GLB loads successfully)
physics_constraints: Fish accelerates at 0.02/frame to max 1.5. Braking reduces speed by 30%/frame to min 0.2. Lateral movement 0.15/frame, clamped to [-18,18]. Tree collision radius 1.5 units. Ring collection radius 2.0 units. Slope length ~500 units.
